chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There was nothing more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) than to remain fearful and hungry for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: What spiritual state was most beloved to the Prophet Muhammad according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the Prophet’s deepest desire was to provide shelter and sustenance to those experiencing 'khawf' (awe/fear) and 'ja’l' (hunger) specifically for God’s sake, linking physical deprivation to spiritual elevation. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere poverty, but as a conscious state of dependence on the Divine, where the believer’s primary concern is their standing before Allah. It underscores the Prophet’s role as a compassionate intercessor who actively facilitates the spiritual comfort of the faithful.
